consequence: RELAY_START_POLICY default stays legacy. The FAIL is kept; any new candidate or rule is a new, separately registered version.
analysis: Fast profile (low noise, J 0.05 s): C1 (graded) improves time-to-start in both series, 4 MiB 6.82 -> 4.66 s and 16 MiB 13.2 -> 9.07 s, matching upstream A (4.71 / 8.98 s); the 16 MiB tail probe drops from ~4.2 s to ~0.05 s. The start-order effect is real where the stalled-peer effect is absent.

Mixed profile (2 stalled of 8 peers): noise J 1.9-11.7 s; C1 medians are mostly lower but no key cell clears J in both series. The registered key cells were all mixed cells, so the stalled-peer effect (SP10) masked the start-order effect: a gate design error, not evidence for C1 being neutral.

Real C1 regressions beyond J: fast/1MiB TTFB +0.20-0.27 s (time-to-start unchanged; graded tail of 4 MiB = 4 urgent-ish tail pieces at 1 MiB pieces), fast/16MiB seek resume +0.25-0.50 s. Mixed-cell regressions are within the noise band of the mixed profile but count under the registered rule.

Upstream A is better than both fork variants in fast/1MiB (TTFB 1.98 s vs 2.6-2.8 s, time-to-start 3.86 vs 4.7 s): the fork's start changes (3+3 urgent boundary pieces, deadlines 0/300/1000+500*d vs upstream 1+1 and 0/2000+1000*d) cost start-up time also at small pieces.
